div.head: II Ew 8
div.ab: Ic wille, þæt ælc gerefa hæbbe gemot á ymbe feower wucan; ⁊ gedon, ðæt ælc man sy folcrihtes wyrðe, ⁊ ðæt ælc spræc hæbbe ende ⁊ andagan, hwænne hit forðcume. Gif hit hwa oferhebbe, bete swa we ær cwædon.

[I]c wylle, þæt ælc gerefa hæbbe gemot a ymbe feower wucan; ⁊ gedon, þæt ælc man sy folcrihtes wyrðe, ⁊ þæt ælc spræc hæbbe ende ⁊ andagan, hwænne hit forþcume. Gyf hit hwa oferhebbe, bete swa we ær cwædon.

Uolo, ut omnis prepositus habeat gemotum semper ad IIII ebdomadas; et efficiat, ut omnis homo publicum rectum habeat; et omne placitum capiat et terminum, quando proueniat, et finem. Si quis hoc excipiat, emendet sicut ante dictum est.

[Be gemote andagum.] Ic wille, þæt ælc gerefa hæbbe gemot á ymbe feower wucan; ⁊ gedon ðæt ælc man sy folcrihtes wyrðe, ⁊ ðæt ælc spræc hæbbe ende ⁊ andagan, hwænne hit forðcume. Gif hit hwa oferhebbe, bete swa we ær cwædon.

(Von den Terminen der Gerichte. Ld) Ich will, dass jeder Gerichtsvogt immer je nach vier Wochen Gerichtsversammlung halte; und [die Vögte] sollen bewirken, dass jedermann Volksrechtes theilhaftig werde, und dass jede Klagesache Ende und Termin habe, wann sie zum Schlusse komme. Wenn einer [der Vögte] das versäumt, büsse er so, wie wir vorher bestimmt haben.

(Of the terms of the courts. Ld) I will that every reeve hold a court-meeting always every four weeks; and [the reeves] are to bring it about that everyone shares in folk-right, and that every suit have an end and a term, when it is to come to its conclusion. If anyone [of the reeves] neglects that, let him pay compensation as we determined before.

It is my will that every reeve shall hold a meeting every four weeks; and they shall see to it that every man obtains the benefit of the public law, and that every suit shall have a day assigned to it on which it shall be heard and decided. And if anyone neglects [to do] this he shall pay such compensation as we have already ordained.

div.note: Liebermann compares I Ew Prol. and II Ew 2. In both H and B, I Edmund follows in the same hand. The initial ‘I’ in B was left for a red capital that was never filled in.

ἓν διὰ δυοῖν f. ‘Endtermin’; vgl. Toller: endedæg, -dogor, -tima ‘Lebensende’
ἓν διὰ δυοῖν for ‘final term’; cf. Toller: endedæg, -dogor, -tima ‘end of life’
Bessere Übs.: ‘wann es [das Urteil] zur Erfüllung (Leistung) komme’ nicht nach Q ‘vorkomme’
Better translation: ‘when it [the judgment] comes to fulfilment (performance)’, not ‘occurs’ as in Q
Kap. 8 wendet sich an Vögte, nicht Parteien; grammatisch freilich bleibt möglich, mit Q und Schmid hwa allgemein ‘jemand’, hit als gemot zu verstehn; das Zitat wäre dann I Ew 1. II 1, 1

Cap. 8 is addressed to the reeves, not to the parties; grammatically, it is true, it remains possible, with Q and Schmid, to take hwa generally as ‘anyone’ and hit as gemot; the citation would then be I Ew 1. II 1, 1
excipere heisst anderswo wohl ‘Einwendungen machen’, aber nicht ‘vernachlässigen’
Elsewhere excipere does mean ‘to raise objections’, but not ‘to neglect’

This would seem to be a meeting comparable to the meeting of the hundred in later times, cf. I Edg. cap. 1. It is doubtful however if the hundred itself as an organised unit was in existence at this time, since the first reference to it is in III Edm. cap. 2.
